name: XO

profile.address: 1928, East Deere Avenue, Dyer, Santa Ana, Orange County, California, 92705
profile.reading:
The building recorded as the Xo Communications Colocation Data Center sits at 1928 East Deere Avenue in Santa Ana, in the Dyer industrial and office corridor of Orange County, California, an area of light industrial and telecommunications buildings near Interstate 405, State Route 55, and John Wayne Airport that has long attracted network and equipment companies because of its central Orange County location and highway access.

XO Communications was a competitive telecommunications carrier that traced its roots to Nextlink Communications, founded in the 1990s and renamed XO Communications in 2002. For most of its independent history the company was majority owned by investor Carl Icahn, and it built a nationwide fiber network offering broadband data, voice, Ethernet, and MPLS services to business customers, along with colocation space in a number of markets as part of its network footprint, this Santa Ana building among them. In 2016, Verizon agreed to acquire XO Communications' fiber optic network and enterprise services business, a deal that closed in early 2017, while XO's separate wireless spectrum holdings were sold off through a different transaction. Following the acquisition, XO's retail and enterprise service lines, including its colocation product, were folded into Verizon's own network and enterprise business over the following years, and the XO brand was retired from active marketing.

Because of that history, no current operator publishes a spec sheet for this Santa Ana building under the XO name today. The facility's continued labeling as an XO Communications colocation data center on public maps and records reflects its origin during XO's era as an independent carrier rather than an actively marketed, separately branded facility in the present day. Whether the space still functions as network infrastructure within Verizon's broader Southern California footprint, has been repurposed, or sits vacant is not confirmed by any public source available for this building specifically. That gap in current, first party information is itself a common outcome when a mid sized regional colocation footprint is absorbed into a much larger national carrier's network, since individual legacy buildings often stop being marketed or documented as standalone facilities once they become one node among many in a larger company's infrastructure, and this particular building is a modest example of that pattern rather than an exception to it.

profile.address: XO Fremont, 47913;47923;47963, Warm Springs Boulevard, Warm Springs District, Fremont, Alameda County, California, 94539
profile.reading:
The building known as XO Fremont sits along Warm Springs Boulevard in the Warm Springs district of Fremont, in Alameda County, California, an industrial and light manufacturing corridor at the southern end of the city that sits near the former NUMMI automobile plant site, now home to Tesla's primary vehicle factory, and within the broader San Francisco Bay Area technology and logistics belt that stretches from San Jose through Fremont toward Oakland.

XO Communications, the building's namesake operator, was a competitive telecommunications carrier that grew out of Nextlink Communications, founded in the 1990s and rebranded as XO Communications in 2002. For much of its history as an independent company, XO was majority owned by investor Carl Icahn and operated a nationwide fiber network delivering broadband, voice, Ethernet, and MPLS services to business customers, supplemented by colocation space in select markets, including this Fremont location, as part of its overall network footprint reaching into the Bay Area. In 2016, Verizon agreed to acquire XO's fiber optic network and enterprise services business in a deal that closed in early 2017, while XO's wireless spectrum assets were divested separately. After the acquisition, XO's retail service lines, including colocation, were absorbed into Verizon's own enterprise and network operations over the following years, and the XO brand was phased out of active use.

As a result, there is no current, first party XO or Verizon page publishing operating specifications, capacity, or tenancy for this specific Fremont building. Its continued appearance under the XO name in public mapping data reflects the period when XO operated it as an independently branded facility rather than its status today. The Warm Springs corridor itself has become a notable node in the Bay Area's data center and industrial real estate market in the years since, with several colocation and network facilities operated by other companies located nearby along the same boulevard, which suggests the area's underlying appeal, land availability, proximity to fiber routes, and access to Bay Area business customers, has outlasted XO's own presence there even if this particular building's current status is not documented in any available public source.

profile.corporate_lineage: XO Communications (HQ Herndon, VA) acquired by Verizon (closed 2016-2017). Verizon subsequently sold 29 legacy data centers (MCI/UUNET/XO heritage) to Equinix for $3.6B, closed May 2017.

reading:
XO Communications was a competitive carrier assembled out of the wreckage of the late 1990s telecommunications boom, headquartered in Herndon, Virginia, selling fibre transport and enterprise data services and running colocation space inside its own switch and point of presence buildings. Verizon bought XO's fibre network and enterprise business in a transaction that closed in 2017, and the XO brand was retired afterwards. This registry keeps the historical name because deleting an operator that once ran a building loses the building's history.

The entry is a good example of why carrier rows need checking rather than counting. Two California rows sit under XO. The first is XO Fremont on Warm Springs Boulevard in Alameda County, mapped across three street numbers, 47913, 47923 and 47963. A public records aggregation of California facility filings lists 47923 Warm Springs Boulevard with Verizon as operator and XO Communications Inc as the original owner, at 1.639 MW of utility power supporting 0.983 MW of IT load, a power usage effectiveness of 1.67, and Pacific Gas and Electric as the serving utility. Those are plausible figures for a carrier building of that vintage and the ratio between them is instructive, but the permit dates in that record read as placeholders, so it is treated here as indicative rather than as a filed fact.

The second row is more clearly a mistag. It is named Xo Communications Colocation Data Center and sits at 1928 East Deere Avenue in Santa Ana, in Orange County. Commercial property listings describe that address as a 12,241 square foot office building, one of six buildings in Alton Deere Plaza, a two storey class B office park of about 188,714 square feet in total. The map record carries no operator tag at all, so the attribution to XO in this registry rests on the building's name string and nothing else. A carrier suite inside a small office park is a real thing, and XO did sell colocation from exactly that kind of space, but a 12,000 square foot class B office suite is not a purpose built data centre and should not be counted as one in a facility total.

One question left open in the earlier version of this record can now be closed. Equinix completed the purchase of 29 data centres from Verizon on 1 May 2017 for 3.6 billion dollars, and the published list covers fifteen metros, including five Silicon Valley sites, SV13 in San Jose and SV14 through SV17 in Santa Clara. Neither Fremont nor Santa Ana appears anywhere on that list, so neither of these two rows transferred to Equinix in that transaction, and their post 2017 ownership remains with Verizon or a later buyer this research did not identify.
